description: Controlled LorentzFM baseline for resume-to-job recommendation. Evaluated against SBERT and BERT under identical data split, candidate job pool, relevance labels, and ranking metrics. This experiment is fully isolated and does NOT modify the CareerCompass AI production pipeline.

dataset.source: LinkedIn Job Postings Dataset (shared across all baselines)

resumes.note: Text formatted as: summary + ' ' + tech_skills + ' ' + current_role (consistent with BERT and SBERT baselines)

jobs.note: job_id is the primary key linking postings, skills, industries and domain labels

split.strategy: Identical stratified split used by BERT and SBERT baselines
split.note: Test split is FIXED. Must NOT be used during training or hyperparameter tuning.

relevance_definition.description: A job is relevant to a resume if and only if the dot product of their 15-dimensional domain label vectors is greater than zero (i.e., they share at least one common domain label).
relevance_definition.note: This is IDENTICAL to the ground truth definition used for SBERT and BERT baselines. Must NOT be changed.

features.description: Structured features to be used by LorentzFM. These are the available features confirmed present in the dataset.

domain_vector.description: 15-dimensional binary domain label vector (primary semantic signal)

skill_count.description: Number of technical skills extracted from resume

resume_features.note: Domain vector (15) + skill_count (1) + seniority_level (1) + education_score (1) + cert_count (1) = 19 dims

domain_vector.description: 15-dimensional binary domain label vector (primary semantic signal)

skill_vector.description: 35-dimensional multi-hot skill code vector (from job_skills.csv + skills mapping)

has_salary.description: Binary indicator: job has salary info

domain_count.description: Number of domain labels assigned to this job

job_features.note: Domain vector (15) + skill vector (35) + experience_level (1) + has_salary (1) + domain_count (1) = 53 dims

model.description: Each structured feature field is embedded separately into Lorentz (hyperbolic) space. Feature interactions are computed on the hyperboloid manifold using the Lorentz inner product. Final score is a compatibility scalar for ranking.
model.interaction: Lorentz inner product sum over all cross-field feature pairs
model.scoring: Sum of Lorentz inner products → scalar compatibility score
model.normalization: All embeddings projected onto Lorentz hyperboloid after initialization
model.note: No SBERT embeddings. No CareerCompass multi-task heads. Pure structured-feature LorentzFM baseline.

negative_sampling.strategy: random in-batch negatives from training job pool (train split only)
negative_sampling.sampling_from: train split jobs only (NOT val or test)

training.note: Validation set used ONLY for early stopping / model selection. Test set is NEVER touched during training.

evaluation.protocol: Identical to SBERT and BERT baselines
evaluation.candidate_pool: All 123849 jobs in postings.csv (same as SBERT/BERT)

isolation_note: LorentzFM code is fully isolated inside lorentzfm_experiment/. It does NOT modify SBERT, BERT, or the CareerCompass AI production model in any way.
